Can A New Open Photo File Format Replace JPEGs?

Nah, JPEG is good enough that slightly better quality is never going to be worth giving up the ubiquitous support. It'll see niche adoption (such as for image database sites like 500px where they have a strong reason for needing something better) but JPEG will remain the default image format for photograph-like images, just like MP3 will remain the default format for music files. It's not that we can't do better, it's just that we can't do better enough that it's worth peoples' while to switch.

I would like to see a new open format that offered good compression that can be set to lossless when needed and supports layers and at least 8 bits of transparency (alpha). The TIFF format had some of this but it was a heavy format and not supported very widely. I also used to like the Targa (.tga) format for quality but it was hardly supported by anything at all. Something new more like PNG with variable compression and layer support would be awesome especially if it could be portable enough to cross devices and color models without being too heavy. We need something that can become as ubiquitous as JPEG but without the industry control. PNG was a step in the right direction but it did not go far enough.
